topic: Types, Anatomy, and Propagation of Waves
key_concepts: Waves are periodic disturbances that move away from a source and carry energy
Transverse waves vibrate perpendicular to the direction of wave travel
Longitudinal waves vibrate parallel or back-and-forth to the direction of wave travel
Surface waves combine transverse and longitudinal motion with particles moving in circular
Mechanical waves need a solid, liquid, or gas medium to propagate
Electromagnetic waves do not need a medium and include radio waves, microwaves, ultraviole
The crest is the highest point and the trough is the lowest point of a transverse wave
Amplitude is the maximum displacement of a particle from its normal position
Wavelength is the distance between adjacent crests or troughs
Frequency is the number of waves passing a point per unit time and is measured in Hertz
Wave speed is related to frequency and wavelength
